## Who

I am Virgile Dine, a PhD student working on **machine unlearning**: given a model trained on a
dataset $\D$ and a forget set $\Df \subset \D$, how do we produce a model that is
statistically indistinguishable from one retrained from scratch on
$\Dr = \D \setminus \Df$ — without paying the cost of full retraining?

## Why this site

Research notes rot when they live in a private notebook. This blog is an attempt
to keep them:

- **Dated** — so I can reconstruct how an idea evolved.
- **Formalised** — every idea gets at least one honest equation.
- **Cited** — claims point at `references.bib`, which feeds straight into the
  thesis bibliography.
- **Reusable** — the section structure of each post maps onto a thesis subsection.

## Research interests

- Certified / provable unlearning and its differential-privacy connections
- Approximate unlearning: influence functions, Newton steps, gradient ascent
- Evaluating forgetting: membership inference as an audit, not a metric
- Unlearning in large language models and diffusion models
- The tension between unlearning, fairness, and model utility

## Colophon

Built with [Quarto](https://quarto.org), written in Markdown + LaTeX, versioned
with Git, and deployed automatically to GitHub Pages via GitHub Actions.
